brief.greeting: Good morning. Hackers turned a fish tank into a pocket, and a keypad into a plug‑and‑play USB gizmo.

stories.headline: Modular macro keypad simplifies USB hardware
stories.body: **Plug‑and‑play macro board:** Hackaday shows a keypad built around the ATmega32U4, which folds the USB controller into the MCU for a lean design.
stories.why: You can drop a custom macro pad into any PC without extra chips.

stories.headline: GDB 18.1 adds env and history tweaks
stories.body: **Debugger gets new knobs:** GDB 18.1 introduces commands to tweak subprocess environments and to persist command‑history to a file, easing repeatable sessions.
stories.why: Your breakpoints stay useful across restarts, and scripts can set up child processes on the fly.

stories.headline: TeleOCR hits 26k downloads on HF
stories.body: **Image‑to‑text goes viral:** StarDoc‑AI’s TeleOCR model has been pulled 26,152 times and earned 468 likes on Hugging Face, proving demand for on‑device OCR.
stories.why: You can embed a ready‑made OCR into edge devices without training your own model.

quick_hits.text: **PDA hack:** Cheap Yellow Display ESP32 turned into a DIY digital assistant.
**Boot lock:** Raspberry Pi firmware now refuses to start with non‑original RAM.
**Fish tank:** Pocket‑sized virtual aquarium fits in your jeans.
**DevOps prep:** Repo aggregates Linux, Jenkins, AWS interview questions.
**Wi‑Fi audit:** USB‑only wifit3 brings cross‑platform Wi‑Fi cracking.

brief.sign_off: Catch you tomorrow, and keep those circuits humming.

highlights.title: A Modular Macro Keypad
highlights.summary: Hackaday article describes a modular macro keypad built around the ATmega32U4 microcontroller, which integrates a USB controller for simpler hardware design.
highlights.detail: The ATmega32U4 enables direct USB communication without extra chips, reducing component count and firmware complexity. The design emphasizes plug‑in modules for customizable key layouts, targeting hobbyists and ergonomic keyboard enthusiasts.

highlights.title: Cheap Yellow Display Dreams of PDA
highlights.summary: Hackaday showcases a portable digital assistant built from a Cheap Yellow Display ESP32 board, turning it into a DIY PDA.
highlights.detail: The project leverages the ESP32's Wi‑Fi and Bluetooth alongside the low‑cost yellow LCD to run simple productivity apps. It demonstrates how inexpensive hardware can be repurposed for handheld computing.

related.title: Audio Spectrum Analyzer on an ESP32 Display Board

highlights.title: The Least Annoying of All Evils
highlights.summary: A recent Raspberry Pi firmware update adds a boot lock that prevents startup when non‑original RAM chips are detected.
highlights.detail: The change aims to improve hardware compatibility and security, but may affect users with third‑party memory modules. Workarounds involve flashing older firmware or using approved RAM.

highlights.title: GDB 18.1 released
highlights.summary: GDB version 18.1 has been released, adding commands for subprocess environment manipulation and command‑history file saving.
highlights.detail: The update also introduces support for new target architectures and expands the Python API, enhancing scripting capabilities for developers debugging complex applications.

highlights.title: bregman-arie/devops-exercises
highlights.summary: The devops-exercises repository aggregates interview questions covering Linux, Jenkins, AWS, and related DevOps tools.
highlights.detail: Targeted at job candidates, the collection includes topics on monitoring, containerization, cloud platforms, and infrastructure as code, providing a comprehensive study resource for technical interviews.

items.title: Model: StarDoc-AI/TeleOCR
items.summary: StarDoc-AI released TeleOCR model on Hugging Face, a image-to-text system that has been downloaded 26,152 times and received 468 likes.
items.detail: TeleOCR converts images containing text into plain text output, supporting a range of document types. It is part of the image-text-to-text category on HF and is gaining traction among developers for OCR tasks.

items.title: Model: nvidia/Nemotron-3-Diarization
items.summary: Nvidia's Nemotron-3-Diarization model for voice activity detection is trending on Hugging Face with 19,620 downloads and 379 likes.
items.detail: The model segments audio streams by detecting speaker changes, useful for transcription pipelines. It belongs to the voice-activity-detection family and reflects Nvidia's push into speech processing tools.

items.title: A Pocket-Sized Digital Fish Tank
items.summary: A pocket-sized digital fish tank prototype demonstrates a virtual aquarium that fits in a pocket without water or live fish.
items.detail: The device uses a small display and embedded controller to simulate fish movement, offering a low-power, portable alternative to traditional aquariums. It avoids the maintenance issues of real fish while providing a visual novelty for hobbyists.

items.title: Basically, Galvanizing Metal Without Acid
items.summary: A new method enables galvanizing steel and iron without using acid, reducing corrosion risk.
items.detail: The technique employs alternative chemical processes that avoid hazardous acids, making rust prevention safer for industrial applications. It expands the toolbox for metal treatment while minimizing environmental impact.

items.title: derv82/wifit3
items.summary: The wifit3 project offers a USB-only, cross‑platform version of the Wifite Wi‑Fi auditing tool.
items.detail: Designed for portability, it runs on multiple operating systems without requiring a full Linux environment, simplifying wireless security testing on the go.

items.title: dream-num/univer
items.summary: The univer repository provides an Office‑style runtime that integrates AI agents with spreadsheets, docs, slides, and PDFs.
items.detail: By unifying common office formats into a single execution environment, it enables AI workflows that can read, write, and manipulate diverse document types programmatically.

items.title: envoyproxy/envoy
items.summary: Envoy is a cloud‑native, high‑performance proxy for edge, middle, and service networking.
items.detail: Implemented in C++, Envoy supports advanced routing, observability, and extensibility, making it a core component in modern microservice architectures.

items.title: esphome/esphome
items.summary: ESPHome provides configuration‑driven control for ESP32, ESP8266, BK72xx, and RP2040 devices, enabling remote management via Home Automation platforms.
items.detail: The system uses simple YAML files to define device behavior, supporting sensors, actuators, and custom code. It abstracts hardware details, allowing engineers to focus on integration rather than low‑level programming. ESPHome runs on the devices themselves, eliminating the need for a separate gateway.

items.title: feigeCode/navop
items.summary: navop is a native Rust workspace that combines database access, SSH, SFTP, terminal, remote desktop, monitoring, and AI tools into a single application.
items.detail: It aims to replace multiple separate utilities with an integrated UI, streamlining workflows for developers and sysadmins. The tool supports a variety of database drivers and includes AI assistance for command generation. Being written in Rust, it targets safety and performance on desktop platforms.
